problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations, in the given order, are to be applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A:$

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2},\,{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}
$$

Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.

activity_context.topic_title: Row Operations on 2x2 Matrices as Products of Elementary Matrices

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix Product That's Equivalent To a Sequence of Row Operations
examples.problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations, in the given order, are to be applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2, \qquad  R_2:=R_2+3R_1
$$

Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
examples.worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the two given elementary row operations.

- The first elementary row operation is $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second elementary row operation is $R_2:=R_2+3R_1.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by $E_1$ on the left and get $E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14058391/assets/d35cb368b7380f08e486757813138fa3f3332ed40a9b0e5faeab7a20c3119bef.png)

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to $E_1 A,$ we multiply by $E_2$ on the left and get $E_2 E_1 A\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14058391/assets/c87dbe6c81a670dd62d8a130d3085b2e9b36d5d3ad27d53bda571ec69b639689.png)

feedback.problem: Suppose we are applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+16{R}_{1}$ to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A.$ Find the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication.
feedback.worked_solution:
We need to find an elementary matrix $E$ such that $EA$ is equivalent to applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+16{R}_{1}$ to $A.$ 

To find $E,$ we apply the given row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+16{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 16 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication is $EA:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 16 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$
